sources.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415v6
sources.locator: §1.2.2 (global phase and projective outcome probabilities, printed pp. 4–5); §1.3 (bipartite pure-state entanglement/product criterion, printed p. 8); §1.4 (CNOT, printed pp. 9–10); §2.1.2 (controlled circuits, Toffoli, inverse circuits, printed pp. 14–15); Exercises 2.2–2.3 and 2.6 (CZ, SWAP, controlled-U, printed p. 19); Chapter 7 §7.2 reflection discussion (PDF p. 66, printed p. 54).

contents.name: Global phase and finite projective outcome law
contents.support: The text notes equal computational-basis probabilities after a unit-modulus scalar; the item proves the full finite-POVM statement locally.

contents.name: CNOT control/target action
contents.support: The text specifies that the first qubit controls a NOT on the second; all four basis actions are checked locally.

contents.name: Control wire and Toffoli activation
contents.support: The circuit convention distinguishes control wires and target action and defines the two-control Toffoli case; the arbitrary control string and negative-control conjugation are proved locally.

contents.name: CNOT followed by H prepares a Bell state
contents.support: The circuit example motivates the state; the coefficient calculation and non-product proof are supplied locally.

contents.name: Controlled-U circuit construction exercise
contents.support: This treats controlled-U as an explicit circuit construction problem; the item defines an access contract and claims no free black-box implementation.

contents.name: Inverse circuit reverses gate order
contents.support: The text states chronological reversal and inversion of each gate; the adjoint-product identity is proved locally.

contents.name: Controlled-Z and SWAP definitions/exercises
contents.support: The exercises specify CZ on |11> and SWAP on ordered basis states; the matrices and unitarity checks are local.

contents.name: Bipartite product-state criterion for entanglement
contents.support: The text defines entanglement as failure to be a tensor product; the Schmidt-rank equivalence is tied to the planned QC03 theorem and remains supplier-dependent.

contents.name: Grover reflection through a subspace
contents.support: The text uses A=2P_V−I and a state-reflection construction; both signs and access accounting are stated locally.

contents.name: Reflection through the marked subspace and uniform state
contents.support: The geometric description motivates the operators; the finite projector algebra and controlled-sign identity are proved locally.

contents.name: State-reflection formula
contents.support: The source gives 2|U><U|−I; normalization, phase invariance, and the second sign are proved locally.

contents.name: Controlled global-phase witness example
contents.support: The example computes the specific U=I witness directly and refers to the locally proved controlled-phase theorem.

contents.name: Unit-vector outer product and pure-state measurement law
contents.support: The source writes pure-state outcome probabilities using rank-one projectors. The item supplies the self-adjointness, non-negativity, and trace-one proof locally in the root linear-first convention.

contents.name: Controlled phase from a phase gate in the controlled block
contents.support: The source defines single-qubit phase gates and gives the general controlled-U block. The exact CP(theta) diagonal action and its unitary check are proved locally.

sources.title: John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles (updated July 2015)
sources.locator: §2.2.1 (overall versus relative phase, printed pp. 8–9); §2.4.1 (pure bipartite entanglement and Bell state, printed pp. 25–26)

contents.name: Overall phase and relative phase in a qubit superposition
contents.support: The text distinguishes common phase from a relative phase; the ratio and projector calculations are supplied locally.

contents.name: Standalone phase of a normalized pure state
contents.support: The source states physical irrelevance of overall phase; the item proves equality for every defined finite-POVM probability.

contents.name: Bipartite pure-state entanglement and Bell state
contents.support: The text defines nonseparability by non-product form and discusses the Bell vector; Schmidt equivalence and the local CNOT proof are handled in this batch.

contents.name: Bell-state entanglement witness
contents.support: The Bell vector is identified as entangled; its actual CNOT preparation and coefficient-matrix-rank proof are supplied locally.

contents.name: The planning locator 'controlled-spin phase discussion'
contents.reason: The fetched chapter's relevant sections discuss common and relative state phase and entanglement, not a controlled-unitary construction. Controlled-gate support is taken from de Wolf §2.1.2/Exercise 2.6 and Preskill Chapter 6 §6.4 instead.

contents.name: Normalized pure-state vector and ray convention
contents.support: The source states the normalized qubit-vector convention and treats common phase at the ray level. The density-operator positivity and trace calculation are proved locally in the item.

sources.title: John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms (updated November 2020)
sources.locator: §6.1 controlled-R phase gates (printed pp. 12–13); §6.4 Phase Estimation (controlled-U eigenphase witness, printed pp. 18–20); §6.6 Quantum Searching, equations (6.152)–(6.153) and reflection interpretation (PDF pp. 35–36; printed pp. 29–30).

contents.name: A unitary conditioned on a control bit and eigenphase readout
contents.support: The source explicitly assumes controlled access and computes a control superposition from a target eigenvalue; the phase-shift witness and POVM probabilities are derived locally.

contents.name: Controlled-unitary capability is an explicit assumption
contents.support: The phase-estimation construction assumes the controlled operation; it does not infer access from a matrix description.

contents.name: Projector reflection sign I−2P on a marked state
contents.support: The source fixes the opposite sign from R=2P−I in its oracle convention; the batch defines both signs explicitly.

contents.name: Reflection through a one-dimensional subspace
contents.support: The source gives a rank-one reflection action; the complete finite projector proof is local.

contents.name: Controlled eigenphase outcome witness
contents.support: The source motivates control-phase readout; the example uses U=I and computes both probabilities locally.

contents.name: Controlled relative phase gate
contents.support: The source describes controlled-R gates that put a phase on the joint |11> component. The local item fixes the exact two-qubit diagonal convention and proves it is unitary.
